name: bool-is-implicit
why: operator bool is not explicit: a Vec2 converts silently to bool and int.

edits.old: explicit operator bool() const { return x_ != 0 || y_ != 0; }
edits.new: operator bool() const { return x_ != 0 || y_ != 0; }

name: bool-only-checks-x
why: a vector like (0, 5) counts as zero.

edits.old: explicit operator bool() const { return x_ != 0 || y_ != 0; }
edits.new: explicit operator bool() const { return x_ != 0; }

name: bool-uses-and
why: (3, 0) counts as zero: && instead of ||.

edits.old: explicit operator bool() const { return x_ != 0 || y_ != 0; }
edits.new: explicit operator bool() const { return x_ != 0 && y_ != 0; }

name: default-vector-is-uninitialized
why: x_ and y_ have no initial value, so a default Vec2 holds garbage.

edits.old:
int x_ = 0;
    int y_ = 0;
edits.new:
int x_;
    int y_;

name: dot-product-is-wrong
why: dot multiplies x by y.

edits.old: inline int dot(const Vec2& a, const Vec2& b) { return a.x() * b.x() + a.y() * b.y(); }
edits.new: inline int dot(const Vec2& a, const Vec2& b) { return a.x() * b.y() + a.y() * b.x(); }

name: equality-only-compares-x
why: operator== ignores y.

edits.old: friend bool operator==(const Vec2&, const Vec2&) = default;
edits.new: friend bool operator==(const Vec2& a, const Vec2& b) { return a.x_ == b.x_; }

name: equality-only-compares-y
why: operator== ignores x.

edits.old: friend bool operator==(const Vec2&, const Vec2&) = default;
edits.new: friend bool operator==(const Vec2& a, const Vec2& b) { return a.y_ == b.y_; }

name: print-format-is-wrong
why: prints (x,y) without the space.

edits.old: inline std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& os, const Vec2& v) { return os << '(' << v.x() << ", " << v.y() << ')'; }
edits.new: inline std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& os, const Vec2& v) { return os << '(' << v.x() << ',' << v.y() << ')'; }

name: print-has-a-space-before-the-comma
why: prints (x , y).

edits.old: inline std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& os, const Vec2& v) { return os << '(' << v.x() << ", " << v.y() << ')'; }
edits.new: inline std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& os, const Vec2& v) { return os << '(' << v.x() << " , " << v.y() << ')'; }

name: print-returns-void
why: operator<< does not return the stream, so it cannot be chained.

edits.old: inline std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& os, const Vec2& v) { return os << '(' << v.x() << ", " << v.y() << ')'; }
edits.new: inline void operator<<(std::ostream& os, const Vec2& v) { os << '(' << v.x() << ", " << v.y() << ')'; }

name: scalar-times-vector-missing
